newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Canal Plus shares jump on Nethold value.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Canal Plus shares jump on Nethold value.

text.p: Shares in French pay-television company Canal Plus jumped by over 2.5 percent on Wednesday on the back of a company report valuing the assets of merger partner Nethold BV at more than 10 billion francs ($1.8 billion).

Canal Plus is set to become Europe's biggest pay-television group on April 15 when it finalises a merger with Dutch-registered media group Nethold after key shareholders' meetings at Canal Plus and major shareholder Havas on March 28.
The market knew that Canal Plus would give Nethold's owners -- Cie Financiere Richemont AG of Switzerland and MIH Holdings of South Africa -- a 20 percent stake and $45 million in cash.
But it did not know the value of assets at Nethold, a loss-making company that was expected to weigh on Canal Plus' 1997 results.

According to a Canal Plus report prepared for the March 28 shareholders meeting, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, the total value of Nethold assets is between 10.725 billion and 12.175 billion francs.
Canal Plus' shares traded at 1330 GMT at 1,159 francs, up almost 2.6 percent.

Nethold, led by South African Johann Rupert, has television assets in the Netherlands, Scandinavia, Italy and other countries, valued at between 8.9 and 10.35 billion francs, or between 7,725 and 8,985 francs per subscriber.
Canal Plus will issue 6.1 million new shares to Nethold in exchange for the assets. Brokers said the valuations were encouraging for Canal Plus shareholders.
Havas will be the biggest shareholder in the merged Canal Plus with a 34.4 percent stake following a transaction with Cie Generale des Eaux in early February.
On Monday, Havas said in a statement it had struck a shareholders pact with Richemont to shield Canal Plus from hostile take-over bids.
According to the Canal Plus report, the net asset value of Nethold after deduction of debts is between 7.125 billion francs and 8.575 billion francs.

The company has a 45 percent stake in Italy's digital television company Telepiu, with Germany's Kirch Gruppe having another 45 percent while Italy's Silvio Berlusconi holds 10 percent through FinInvest SpA.
The Canal Plus report put the value of Telepiu at $2.0 billion. The report said the Italian group was currently "heavily loss-making" due to strong investment in new digital technology.
The report valued at 1.825 billion francs Nethold's 6.45 percent stake in Italian commercial broadcaster Mediaset SpA.
Nethold as a whole is also losing money, and the report said it expected the company to break even on operating income at the end of 1999.
Financial analysts estimate the merger will reduce Canal Plus's 1997 earnings by about 600 million francs. ($ = 5.683 French Francs)
